thread.title: World Calendar October 16, 2025

author: Guest
title: World Calendar October 16, 2025
text:
Oct. 16
Halloween Trivia Night at Stowe Free Library — Trivia will be rain or shine! If it’s nice weather, trivia will be on the lawn. If it’s not nice, we’ll have an adventure and have trivia in the stacks. 5:30-6:30 p.m. Stowe Free Library, 90 Pond St., Stowe. 802-253-6145.
Oct. 17
Autumn Rummage Sale — 9-6 p.m. Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier.
Champlain Valley Craft Show and Antique Expo — Handmade Treasures & Timeless Finds Await at the Expo! 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Champlain Valley Exposition, 105 Pearl St., Essex. 603-332-2616.
Moonlight Magic — Celebrate the season early during Montpelier’s Moonlight Magic. Enjoy downtown shopping deals, festive entertainment, dining, and holiday cheer, all while supporting local businesses. 4-8 p.m. Montpelier. 802-282-2163.
Feed My Starving Children MobilePack — Turn hunger to hope by packing life-saving meals for starving children. 5-4:30 p.m. Albert D Lawton Intermediate, 104 Maple St., Essex Junction. 802-777-8349.
‘Stardust’ Talk — Constellations & Cultures with Mariama Jones from the Fairbanks Museum. 5:30-7 p.m. Mad River Valley Arts, 5031 Main St., Waitsfield. 802-496-6682.
Senior Center Singers — 7-10 p.m. American Legion, Post 63, 48 Depot Square, Northfield.
Oct. 18
Bag Sale — Bag Sale 9 a.m.-1 p.m. Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier.
Dog River Day — The event highlights the charms and value of this unique river, informs about the challenges faced by the river and those who love it and live near or on it. Noon-3 p.m. Northfield.
No Thrones, No Crowns, NO KINGS — We reject strongman politics and corruption and will resist until we get the representation we deserve. Noon-2 p.m. Vermont State House, 115 State St., Montpelier. 714-293-5595.
Vermont Women and the Civil War — Vermont Historian, Howard Coffin tells the story: Vermont Women and The Civil War, Presented in conjunction with The Moretown Historical Society 2-3 p.m. Moretown United Methodist Church, 981 Vermont 100B, Moretown.
Celestial Sounds — 67th Season Opens with Mozart and Holst 4-6 p.m. Highland Center for the Arts, 2875 Hardwick St., Greensboro. 802-279-0003.
Grand Kyiv Ballet Presents Swan Lake — a timeless tale of love and magic brought to life by world-class dancers and Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable music. 7-9 p.m. Chandler Music Hall at Chandler Center for the Arts, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.
Contra Dance at the Grange — with Isaac Banner (Seattle) calling and tunes by Crossover Trio. No partner or experience needed. All dances taught. Gender neutral role terms. Newcomers lesson 7:45 p.m. 7:45-11 p.m. Capital City Grange, 6612 Vermont 12, Berlin. 802-225-8921.
Oct. 19
Drop ’N’ Swap — Annual event at Norwich University, 11 a.m.-3 p.m. Plumley Armory, 24 ID White Ave., Northfield. 802-485-2670.
Celestial Sounds — 67th Season Opens with Mozart and Holst. 2-4 p.m. Barre Opera House, 6 North Main St., Barre. 802-279-0003.
Oct. 20
Warning — Warning Graniteville Fire District No. 4 Annual Meeting, Community Room Quarry Hill Apartments 6:30-10 p.m. Quarry Hill Apartments, 604 Graniteville Road, Barre Town.
Oct. 22
Robin’s Nest Nature Playgroup — is a free activity for families to gather, learn, and play in nature. 10 a.m.-noon. North Branch Nature Center, 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Estate Planning Essentials — Estate planning isn’t just about documents, it’s about making sure your wishes are clear and your family is protected. 5:30-6:30 p.m. The Hub CoWorks, 67 Merchants Row, Rutland. 802-383-6700.
Star-gazing with George Springston — 6:30-8:30 p.m. Jaquith Public Library, 122 School St., Marshfield. 802-426-3581.
Oct. 23
‘Stardust’ talk — How the Earth Rides the Solar Wind’ with Presenters James Slinkman and Josh Kuckens. This talk coincides with the art show ‘Stardust’. 5:30-7 p.m. Mad River Valley Arts, 5031 Main St., Waitsfield. 802-496-6682.
Rapture — A queer feast of dramatic comedy about faith, family, and euphoria. 7-9 p.m. Montpelier Performing Arts Hub, 35 College St., Montpelier. 802-798-6717.
Oct. 25
The Runaway Pumpkin 10K & 5K Run/Walk — Fun for the whole family, the 10th annual Runaway Pumpkin is part of the New Hampshire Pumpkin Festival. Great awards, cash prizes, tech shirts and a Kids Fun Run. 9-11:30 a.m. Opechee Park, 879 North Main Street, Laconia. 603-630-4468.
Barre City Lighting of the Pumpkins Contest — Bring your pre-carved pumpkins to Mathewson Playground in Barre for a chance to win a $50 gift certificate to a restaurant in Barre City. 5 – 6 p.m.
Oct. 26
Capital City Concerts presents — Born in 1685: Bach, Handel & Scarlatti with violinist Ari Issacman-Beck, flutist Karen Kevra, and pianist Jeffrey Chappell mix and match in works by three great composers born the same year. 3-4:30 p.m. Unitarian Church Of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier.
Vermont Friends of Standing Together: Movie premiere of “The Other.” Moderated Discussion; Optional Potluck 4:30-7 p.m. Ohavi Zedek Synagogue, 188 North Prospect Street, Burlington.
Oct. 28
The Fretless and Vasen — The Fretless (Canada) meets Vasen (Sweden) in a high-energy night of virtuosic string music, where tradition and innovation collide in electrifying style. 7-9 p.m. Chandler Music Hall at Chandler Center for the Arts, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.
Oct. 29
Robin’s Nest Nature Playgroup — is a free activity for families to gather, learn, and play in nature. 10 a.m.-noon. North Branch Nature Center, 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Oct. 30
TEDxNewEngland — Join nine extraordinary women to honor New England’s leadership in science and technology, spotlighting the power of diverse perspectives in science, creativity, and human understanding. 7-9 p.m. Groton Hill Music Center, 122 Old Ayer Road, Groton.
Oct. 31
Montpelier Halloween Trick or Treating — Downtown trick or treating in the heart of Montpelier. 4-6 p.m. Montpelier.
Halloween Trick-or-Treating at Brookfield Old Town Hall which will be decorated for Halloween and welcoming trick-or-treaters 4-7 p.m. Brookfield Old Town Hall, 93 Stone Road, Brookfield.
Nov. 5
Robin’s Nest Nature Playgroup — is a free activity for families to gather, learn, and play in nature. 10 a.m.-Noon. North Branch Nature Center, 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Nov. 8
Leroy Preston — Grammy-winning co-founder of Asleep at the Wheel, returns with swing, country, and blues. His latest project The Vermont Sessions features new songs with an all-star band. 7-9 p.m. Chandler Center for the Arts, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.
Nordic Sunrise — Counterpoint joins Eleva Chamber Players at Waterbury Congregational Church, 8 N. Main St, Waterbury, 3 p.m. For tickets: www.elevachamberplayers.com/.
Early Bird Dinner – At The American Legion Post 63, Northfield. Menu: Roast pork, mashed potatoes, vegetable and a roll. Non-member guest $15.
Nov. 9
Nordic Sunrise — Counterpoint joins Eleva Chamber Players at The Inn at the Round Barn Farm, 1661 E Warren Rd, Waitsfield, 3 p.m. For tickets: www.elevachamberplayers.com/.
Nov. 12
Robin’s Nest Nature Playgroup — is a free activity for families to gather, learn, and play in nature. 10 a.m.-noon. North Branch Nature Center, 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Nov.13
Lyric Theatre Co.’s A Chorus Line at The Flynn MainStage, Nov. 13-16 will be presented at The Flynn Main Stage Nov. 13 through 16, 7:30 p.m. The Flynn, 153 Main St., Burlington. 802-658-1484.
